gist: A default is otherwise admissible only for a choice that narrows or keeps things as they are, and every default's cost is on screen
entry_phrase: A default is otherwise admissible only for a choice that narrows or keeps things as they are, and every default's cost is on screen.

gist: Relay offering is on by default for servers and home nodes under the device policy; it carries sealed rows and discloses the route only; it may be turned off
entry_phrase: **Relay offering is the stated exception:** it carries other people's sealed rows and discloses the node's route to a referred stranger, nothing of the person's content or identity. It is on by default for servers and home nodes under the device policy of [CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6), because the mesh does not seat its peers otherwise. It is a choice like the others, its cost on screen, and it may be turned off.

gist: An unanswered choice the node does not need never blocks: it is deferred, nothing leaves on its account, and it waits in the queue
entry_phrase: An unanswered choice that the node does not need in order to run never blocks the person. It is `deferred`, nothing leaves on its account, since nothing leaves without a signed row, and it waits in the queue until answered.

gist: An option that cannot be undone is never a default and is confirmed before signing; a narrowing option takes one step
entry_phrase: An option that cannot be undone is never a default. An item is confirmed before it is signed when the rows it would sign widen or have no way back. Every other item takes one step, so withdrawing, leaving and taking back are one step each.

gist: An outward-writing item answered before a claim is held and not applied, no owner key existing, and lapses if the claim never comes
entry_phrase: An item whose writes leave the node (a grant, a binding, a consent) answered before a claim is held and not applied, since no owner key exists to sign it. Such an item lapses if the claim never comes.

gist: An item writing nothing outward applies at once; the owner's signed row supersedes the local record after the claim
entry_phrase: An item that writes nothing outward (a setting of the node itself, shaping among them) applies at once, because applying it leaks nothing and waiting would, and the owner's signed row supersedes the local record after the claim.

gist: A client renders an item with no node, from the data alone
entry_phrase: A client renders an item with no node, from the data alone.

gist: A client renders two served shapes and nothing else: the view (view.cddl) and the queue
entry_phrase: A client of this document renders two served shapes and nothing else: the **view** (`manifests/view.cddl`) and the **queue**.

gist: The view is one object's rows and the atoms the node folded through the person's policies, each with provenance: the rows read and the rule run
entry_phrase: The view is one object's rows and the atoms the node folded from them through the person's own policies. Each atom carries its provenance, the rows it read and the rule it ran, so that what is true now is always shown beside why.

gist: Every string the client shows is a node-served text reference resolved for the asked locale; the client holds no copy; an unlocalizable string is served in source language, marked
entry_phrase: **Every string the client shows is served by the node as a text reference,** an id with parameters resolved for the locale the client asked for. The client holds no copy of its own. A string the node cannot localize is served in its source language and marked so, never invented.

gist: While a bundle lacks a locale the node serves the reference with source text marked; a consumer may resolve the id from a held bundle, preferring the node's localized text
entry_phrase: **The way there is the same contract:** while a node's bundle lacks a locale it serves the reference with its text in the source language and the language marked. Meanwhile a consumer MAY resolve that id from a bundle it still holds, preferring the node's text whenever the node serves it in the requested locale.

gist: The client holds the deployment's keys (user, node, agent), each signing only its own rows, and no policy; a view is read through the person's trust set
entry_phrase: **The client holds the keys of its deployment and no policy:** the person's own user key and the node's key, and the agent's key where an agent runs. These are two or three hybrid key sets by deployment, each signing only its own rows ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)). A view is read through the person's trust set ([CC 4.4.3.8](#4.4.3.8)) and the client decides nothing the node did not.

gist: For an object the person can see the node holds its family, lifecycle state and the person's standing: author, subject, member, moderator, founder, steward, holder, witness
entry_phrase: For an object the person can see, the node holds the object's family, its lifecycle state, and the person's standing toward it. The standing is the roles the held rows give them: author, subject, member, moderator, founder, steward, holder, witness.

gist: A family's lifecycle is its transitions in the family model, each a verb with states, roles that may sign, governance row and whether it widens
entry_phrase: A family's lifecycle is the transitions of its row in the family model. Each transition is a verb with the state it leaves and reaches, the roles that may sign it, its governance row and whether it widens.

gist: The queue is exactly the transitions enabled for this person in this state, one item each; the door is the same predicate, so queue and door never disagree
entry_phrase: The queue is exactly the transitions enabled for this person in this state, one item each, and an item's writes are the row that transition signs. The admission door is the same predicate, so the queue never offers what the door would refuse and the door never admits what the queue would not have offered.

gist: A stranger to an object sees no item on it; an item that moved the object is gone from the next view
entry_phrase: A stranger to an object sees no item on it. An item that moved the object's state is gone from the next view.

gist: A widening item is confirmed before it is signed and a narrowing one takes one step
entry_phrase: An item that widens or has no way back is confirmed before it is signed, and every other item takes one step.

gist: A node derives the queue from the same held rows and policy it admits by, never from a separate list
entry_phrase: A node derives the queue from the same held rows and the same policy it admits by, never from a separate list.

gist: An item never crosses between nodes; only the rows an answer signs travel; other devices learn by the row; each node keeps its own queue and none is synchronised
entry_phrase: **An item never crosses between nodes:** a node builds it for its own client from the rows it holds, the policy table and the family model, and only the rows an answer signs travel. A person's other devices learn the answer by the row. So each node keeps its own queue, an item clears when its row arrives, and no queue is synchronised.

gist: The queue never blocks: transport carries signed rows and cosignatures and reports a decision row landed; the host decides from the rows which items present
entry_phrase: The queue never blocks: the transport carries signed rows and cosignatures and reports that a decision row landed, and the host decides from the rows which items present themselves.

gist: Community steward names the super-mod tier and is distinct from steward-binding, the owner-to-node relation; the qualified form is used wherever context does not fix it
entry_phrase: **Term pin:** *community steward* is this super-mod tier — distinct from *steward-binding*, the [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) owner→node relation.

gist: The fallback tally is taken over who shows up, the count set a community's policy names; the community routes around an absent moderator
entry_phrase: The tally is taken over **who shows up** — the count set a community's policy names, where the accord's roster change names the standing roster. The community **routes around** an absent moderator.

gist: 48 hours is the shortest span that gives every member in every time zone a weekday to respond; 24 covers one working day and no day off
entry_phrase: Its one job is the legitimacy of the members' majority, and 48 hours is the shortest span that gives every member in every time zone a weekday to respond, where 24 covers one working day and no day off.

gist: The moderator rules on a private report at any time or lets it rest
entry_phrase: The moderator rules on it at any time or lets it rest.

gist: A community must never sit without a moderator, and no node holds a key that could appoint one
entry_phrase: A community must never sit without a moderator, and no node holds a key that could appoint one.

gist: A person's agreeing ballots are one ballot; disagreeing ballots neither withdrawn are no ballot until a withdrawal leaves one; no instant decides
entry_phrase: A person's agreeing ballots are one ballot. Disagreeing ballots neither withdrawn are no ballot until a withdrawal leaves one, and no instant decides.

gist: Nothing signed opens an election, since a lapse by inactivity has no row; the election is named by what every node holds
entry_phrase: Nothing signed opens an election, since a lapse by inactivity has no row. So the election is **named by what every node holds**.

gist: The ballot set an acceptance binds covers the ballot and withdrawal rows held, so the count over it is reproducible; a node's clock closes nothing
entry_phrase: The set covers the ballot and withdrawal rows held, so the count over it is reproducible.

gist: Every node holding the same rows seats the same moderator; nodes holding different rows may seat differently until their rows converge, a residual of the mixed fleet
entry_phrase: every node holding the same rows seats the same moderator. Two nodes that hold different rows, as halves of a fleet do across an edition in which one half admits a removal the other refuses, may seat differently until their rows converge.

gist: The interstitial reads: I consent to view this material reported as a potential infohazard
entry_phrase: The interstitial reads *"I consent to view this material reported as a potential infohazard."*

gist: A lone authority is a single point of capture and of failure; no community is ever hostage to an absent moderator or steward
entry_phrase: A lone authority is a single point of capture and of failure.

gist: The federation's promise is revocability and accountability, not behavioral control; a community that harbors harm is on the record as having done so
entry_phrase: Per [CC 4.2](part_4_composition_governance.md) M-1, the federation's promise here is **revocability and accountability**, not behavioral control. A community that harbors harm is on the record as having done so, and that record is what justice composes over.

gist: The attributable-view ladder is about a viewer who chooses to see kept content, not about adjudication
entry_phrase: The attributable-view ladder above is about a viewer who *chooses* to see kept content. It is not about adjudication.

gist: Moderation is member-reporting plus reverse-quorum adjudication, not substrate scanning of private content: anonymity to outsiders, accountability to insiders
entry_phrase: This is **member-reporting + reverse-quorum adjudication**, *not* substrate scanning of private content.

gist: In the accord a lone survivor fires and the roster is changed by a majority of the standing roster within a window; in moderation a lone steward acts and the live community reconstitutes governance when stewards vanish
entry_phrase: In the accord, a **lone survivor fires** and the roster is changed by a **majority of the standing roster**, cast within a window. In moderation, a **lone steward acts** and, when stewards vanish, the **live community reconstitutes governance**.

gist: The proposal, window and tally ride the participation shape and the action primitives; the consent gate rides the consent family and the content_class flag; no new structural primitive
entry_phrase: The proposal/window/tally rides the generalized [CC 4.2.6](part_4_composition_governance.md) participation shape + the [CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md) action primitives (`moderation:*` / `takedown_notice` / `reconsideration:*`).

gist: A fraction of the base stays reachable at ten thousand members as at ten; the law's constants are provisional until measured
entry_phrase: A fraction therefore stays reachable at ten thousand members as at ten (the law's constants are provisional until measured).

gist: A community may not set its policy laxer than the corridor allows
entry_phrase: It may not set it laxer than the corridor allows.

gist: A signed instant is the signer's to choose, so a window read on it could be shortened in advance or entered after it closed; receipt is the one clock no signer sets
entry_phrase: The reason is that a signed instant is the signer's to choose, and a window read on it could be shortened in advance or entered after it closed. Receipt is the one clock no signer sets.

gist: The view after an admitted row is the fold over the larger set; a node has no second copy of anything to drift
entry_phrase: An admitted row is appended and nothing is rewritten, and the view after is the fold over the larger set.

gist: The preview of a row under a policy of more than one voice says what the fold says: the object's state, unchanged, and what is still missing, the voices or the instant
entry_phrase: So the preview of such a row says what the fold says: the object's state, unchanged, and what is still missing, the voices or the instant.

gist: What a preview claims is exact over the rows the node holds and says nothing about rows it does not hold
entry_phrase: What a preview claims is exact over the rows the node holds.

gist: Each choice is presented the same way, each changes something, and none is more or less a choice than another
entry_phrase: Each is presented the same way, each changes something, and none is more or less a choice than another.

gist: The purpose of a node and its client is to let the person see the current state of the attestations they trust and to put before them, as one queue, what waits on their hand
entry_phrase: It lets the person see the current state of the attestations they trust, through the policies they already hold ([CC 4.4.3.8](#4.4.3.8)). It puts before them, as one queue, what waits on their hand.

gist: The two costs of announcing when declined are those of the announcing section
entry_phrase: The two costs of announcing when declined are those of [CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6).

gist: The record and the state are one thing seen twice: the record is the rows, the state is the node's fold of them, and the outcome of every choice is a row appearing in a view
entry_phrase: The record and the state are one thing seen twice: the record is the rows, the state is the node's fold of them, and the outcome of every choice is a row appearing in a view.

gist: Text ids are one namespace shared by every consumer, so held strings and served ids can be compared
entry_phrase: The ids are one namespace shared by every consumer, so the strings a consumer still holds and the ids a node serves can be compared.

gist: The queue is the door run forwards
entry_phrase: The queue is the door run forwards.

gist: Group-scoped destinations are resolved from a cached directory plus per-group HKDF, never from an announce.
entry_phrase: group destinations are resolved from a **cached directory + per-group HKDF**, never from an announce

gist: A destination whose cohort_scope is below federation (self, family, community, affiliations) never emits a Reticulum announce, directed or broadcast; the substrate suppresses it.
entry_phrase: MUST NOT emit a Reticulum announce, **directed or broadcast**. **The prohibition binds the emission, not the addressing mode.**

gist: Only federation/Commons-scope destinations (species, biosphere, federation, infrastructure opt-out) may announce normally; they carry no anonymity claim.
entry_phrase: Only federation/Commons-scope destinations (`species`, `biosphere`, `federation`, and the `infrastructure` opt-out) MAY announce normally — they carry no anonymity claim.

gist: A node announces when its owner-binding is carried at cohort_scope federation, owner-signed at that audience; a person's public roster is exactly the set of their nodes with federation-scoped owner-bindings.
entry_phrase: The public roster of a person is **exactly the set of their nodes whose owner-binding is federation-scoped**

gist: A fedID with no announced node is reached only by a node code handed by the owner (contact code or QR); no forwarder serves its route, no stranger finds it.
entry_phrase: A fedID with no announced node is reached only by handing its node code directly, a contact code or its QR form passed by the owner's own hand

gist: An unannounced node's owner-signed occurrence and owner binding ride sealed inside the contact request and acceptance, held by the owner's nodes and the contact alone, served by no forwarder.
entry_phrase: The owner-signed identity occurrence and owner-binding that tie the node to its person ride sealed inside the contact request and inside the acceptance.

gist: An unannounced identity cannot join a public group: a public room admits by the joiner's own signature at the Commons tier; an unverifiable key is withheld, not refused.
entry_phrase: An unannounced identity cannot take part in a public group.

gist: A client states the two costs (contact only by handed code; no public group) when announcing is declined.
entry_phrase: These are the two costs a client states when announcing is declined.

gist: Un-announcing is the owner superseding the binding at cohort_scope self and withdrawing the grants that carried it; what others hold they keep; the node becomes unfindable, never unknown.
entry_phrase: **Un-announcing** is the owner superseding the binding at `cohort_scope: self` and withdrawing the grants that carried it to the roots they trust, one act in the client.

gist: The Reticulum announce of a node's transport destination, emitted by every routing node, places nothing on the device roster.
entry_phrase: The Reticulum announce of a node's transport destination, which every routing node emits, places nothing on the roster by itself.

gist: A node holding a serve seat in an infrastructure community has an announced owner: a live owner-binding at cohort_scope federation exists while it holds the seat, requestable any time.
entry_phrase: While the node holds the seat, a live owner-binding for it MUST exist at `cohort_scope: federation`; it need not be part of the genesis and can be requested at any time.

gist: The seat-owner test is evaluated live, never at a past instant: a binding made after seating satisfies it; a withdrawn binding stops satisfying it.
entry_phrase: The test is evaluated live, never at a past instant: a binding made after the node was seated satisfies it, and a withdrawn binding stops satisfying it.

gist: While no federation-scope owner-binding exists a seated node does not serve under the seat, refused serve_seat_owner_unannounced; the check is persist's and the server gates on it.
entry_phrase: While no such binding exists the node does not serve under the seat, refused `serve_seat_owner_unannounced`

gist: A node that boots seated and owned but unannounced announces itself if its owner's key is present and otherwise raises an alarm.
entry_phrase: A node that boots seated and owned but unannounced announces itself if its owner's key is present and otherwise raises an alarm.

gist: A node whose owner-binding is held only at self is reachable by the owner's nodes and v3-code holders, never listed; no directory, serve policy or read route enumerates it.
entry_phrase: A directory, serve policy or read route MUST NOT enumerate it to any node outside the owner's `self` cohort.

gist: A roster is never enumerable outside its cohort; re-signing the binding at federation scope is the opt-in.
entry_phrase: This mirrors the roster discipline (a roster is never enumerable outside its cohort) at the identity plane, where re-signing the binding at federation scope *is* the opt-in.

gist: A node whose owner resolves to the minor band never carries a federation-scope owner-binding; admission refuses the promotion; the minor is reachable only on the derived plane; nothing lifts this.
entry_phrase: So a node whose owner resolves to the `minor` band MUST NOT carry a federation-scope owner-binding, and admission MUST refuse the promotion.

gist: A node offers an identity:occurrence:v1 row to a peer only when it would also relay the attester's federation-announced owner-binding; an unverifiable attester's row is withheld, not served to be refused.
entry_phrase: A node offers an `identity:occurrence:v1` row to a peer only when it would also relay the row's attester key to that peer

gist: An agent attester's key carries a live steward binding and is relayable exactly when its owner-binding is announced, by the per-node rule, like any device of a person.
entry_phrase: it is relayable exactly when its owner-binding is announced, by the per-node rule, no differently from any device of a person's.

gist: Every participating L1 peer maintains a complete local copy of the federation directory's X-Wing public keys, refreshed via federation_keys anti-entropy; the directory stays federation-public.
entry_phrase: Every participating L1 peer maintains a COMPLETE local copy of the federation directory's X-Wing public keys, refreshed via the existing `federation_keys` anti-entropy.

gist: A group destination is resolved deterministically from cached directory entry plus per-group HKDF; every member derives the same; outsiders cannot.
entry_phrase: A group destination is resolved DETERMINISTICALLY from (cached directory entry + per-group HKDF)

gist: No per-invitation or per-resolution directory query is emitted.
entry_phrase: NO per-invitation / per-resolution directory query is emitted.

gist: Phone-class peers that cannot hold the full directory resolve through their L1-relay parent over a relay-blinded path.
entry_phrase: Phone-class peers that cannot hold the full directory resolve through their L1-relay parent over a relay-blinded path.

gist: Destination derivation: S_dest = MLS-Exporter(ciris-scope-destination-v1); k_destination = HKDF-SHA256-Expand(S_dest, destination/v1 label, 32); destination = HKDF-SHA3-256(k_destination, salt empty, label||u32_be(len(member_key_id))||member_key_id, 16).
entry_phrase: The destination is derived per member, per group epoch, from the group's MLS exporter and the member's `key_id` (the cached directory entry).

gist: The expand step is bare HKDF-SHA256-Expand, not RFC 9420 ExpandWithLabel; S_dest is a separate exporter from S_record; storage holds the record secret, only transport holds the destination secret.
entry_phrase: The expand step is bare `HKDF-SHA256-Expand`, not RFC 9420 `ExpandWithLabel`.

gist: A destination is derived once per (group, epoch) at a membership or epoch change, never per packet; it rotates by install-next, activate, seal, never silencing a group.
entry_phrase: A destination is derived once per `(group, epoch)` at a membership or epoch change, never per packet

gist: Announce suppression hides a group's content, membership and address-to-group mapping; it does not hide that a node opens links to derived destinations or the shape of that traffic.
entry_phrase: What this section hides is the group's content, its membership and its address-to-group mapping.

gist: The anonymity target is outsiders holding no cohort envelope, including a subpoena against the directory; in-group members see the group fully; the on-path forwarder claim is 1.13.3.1's.
entry_phrase: The construction hides the group's existence, membership, and `querier → invitee` edges from **outsiders only**

gist: A peer with a stale or incomplete directory cache resolves fewer destinations and reports an honest miss; it never falls back to a group-scoped announce or a per-destination query.
entry_phrase: it MUST NOT fall back to emitting a group-scoped announce or a per-destination query to recover reachability.

gist: Absence of per-destination announce control fails toward suppression, never toward announce.
entry_phrase: its absence MUST fail toward suppression, never toward announce.

gist: A directed (targeted) announce inherits the group-scope prohibition; the object is the emission class, not the broadcast; the targeted per-destination query is banned likewise.
entry_phrase: A targeted announce inherits the prohibition rather than escaping it.

gist: A reading never spends a claimable guarantee (no emission exists) to purchase an unclaimable one (traffic-analysis privacy).
entry_phrase: A reading MUST NOT spend a claimable guarantee to purchase an unclaimable one.

gist: In-group distribution of addressing material over MLS is not an announce and is not prohibited.
entry_phrase: in-group distribution of addressing material over MLS is not an announce and is not prohibited.

gist: Multi-hop reach for a group-scoped destination is an amendment-plane question with the bar: no outsider-observable emission, no outsider-retained path state, no epoch-correlated wave; never a reading of this clause.
entry_phrase: Multi-hop reach for a group-scoped destination is therefore an **amendment-plane design question**

gist: Where no direct path exists a scoped body may ride the members' identity-plane link through a forwarder: end-to-end encrypted, room discriminated inside the link, admitted against the derived-address table.
entry_phrase: a scoped body MAY ride the members' **identity-plane link** on three terms.

gist: A forwarder's sanctioned role is reachability, never custody of the conversation: it carries link ciphertext only and retains nothing beyond the transport table kept for every forwarded link.
entry_phrase: **The intermediary's sanctioned role is reachability, never custody of the conversation.**

gist: Where endpoints can bring the link direct (shared interface or direct dial on an address the path exchange revealed) the link is brought direct and the forwarder drops out.
entry_phrase: the link MUST be brought direct and the forwarder drops out.

gist: A forwarder is never handed anything that names the room.
entry_phrase: and MUST NOT be handed anything that names the room.

gist: A node stands to a frame as an end, as a carrier that said yes (contact offering relay, serve seat, non-opted-out Anonymous Tier relay), or as a stranger.
entry_phrase: A node stands to a frame in one of three ways:

gist: A stranger carries on a shaped link only what needs no consent: link setup and cover; public self-authenticating rows (key records, revocations, occurrences, allegiance, unowned routes); sealed consent asks; halt; tombstones
entry_phrase: A stranger carries, on a shaped link, only what no one must consent to carry:

gist: A row of the stranger-carried set carries no context member and is of bounded size, so a carrier checks what it carries without opening it.
entry_phrase: A row of that set carries no `context` member and is of bounded size, so a carrier can check what it carries without opening it.

gist: A scoped body (room body, live stream chunks included) crosses a forwarder only one that said yes, a consented contact or last-resort serve seat; a stranger is offered none.
entry_phrase: A scoped body, a room body and a live stream's chunks included, crosses a forwarder only one that has said yes, a consented contact or, as last resort, a serve seat; a stranger is offered none.

gist: An Anonymous Tier relay is a carrier that said yes, carrying a fixed-length packet it cannot read; it is a relay, not a forwarder; the forwarder rule misses it.
entry_phrase: It is a relay, not a forwarder, and the forwarder rule does not reach it.

gist: Carriage is a property of the link, not its class: any link may be set consent-only, including between two serve seats; the two ends or a consenting carrier choose it.
entry_phrase: Carriage is a property of the link and not of its class

gist: Nothing narrows what two ends send each other; every road to a consent (first contact, adding a device, joining a room, halt, key revocation) runs on strangers alone.
entry_phrase: Nothing in this rule narrows what the two ends send each other.

gist: A consenting forwarder may carry a live stream's chunks between two members lacking a direct path; never a fan-out node of the relay tree, buffering only the frame, no binding.
entry_phrase: MAY carry one member's link to another member when no direct path exists.

gist: A publisher's stream binding and each chunk's authentication are verified by members, the tree's relays and receivers, never by a forwarder.
entry_phrase: A publisher's binding and each chunk's authentication are verified by members, the tree's relays and the receivers, never by a forwarder.

gist: The stream binding fixes the tree root: the named publisher is the only member at depth zero; an offer claiming depth zero from another key or before the binding drops.
entry_phrase: The binding also fixes the tree's root: the publisher it names is the only member at depth zero

gist: A substrate prefers the derived address whenever a direct link exists and never routes a scoped body through a forwarder when a direct path is available.
entry_phrase: A substrate MUST prefer the derived address whenever a direct link exists and MUST NOT route a scoped body through a forwarder when a direct path is available.

gist: Minors are unaffected by forwarding: reachability still requires the federation-scope announce a minor's node cannot carry.
entry_phrase: Minors are unaffected: reachability still requires the announce a minor's node cannot carry (the device-roster rule above).

gist: A peer that wants to be reachable publishes its owner binding at federation scope; a stranger reaches it by its federation identity and the first message crosses a forwarder.
entry_phrase: A peer that wants to be reachable publishes its owner-binding at federation scope (the public roster above).

gist: An owned node's signed route is handed by its owner and never served by a forwarder.
entry_phrase: **An owned node's signed route is handed by its owner and never served by a forwarder.**

gist: Offering relay is handing the node's route to strangers for first contact and consent, three at a time to peers a full node refuses; relay off reports no capacity.
entry_phrase: An owner who offers relay hands the node's route to strangers for first contact and consent, three at a time to peers a full node refuses

gist: Relay is offered by default on every owned node; turning it off is the owner's choice made with its cost on screen (the node carries nobody, refers nobody).
entry_phrase: **Relay is offered by default on every owned node**, the shaped mesh standing on it.

gist: A referred peer is a proxy: it serves the asker from what it holds, pulling a missing federation-tier row from the seat as its own pull; non-federation rows never proxied.
entry_phrase: A peer that a seat or a full node referred an asker to serves the asker from what it holds.

gist: A proxy is an offering node under its public identity, named in referrals with its route; an anonymous node proxies nothing and relays nothing; wanting both means two nodes.
entry_phrase: A proxy is an offering node under its public identity, named in referrals with its route.

gist: A phone offers relay while charging on an unmetered network and reports no capacity otherwise; a node reporting no capacity is never referred and never counted as a parent.
entry_phrase: A phone offers relay while it is charging on an unmetered network and reports no capacity otherwise

gist: A route rides inside the sealed first-contact request and sealed acceptance; a forwarder serves an owned node's route to nobody, holds no contact grant, never gets the consent readable.
entry_phrase: A forwarder serves an owned node's route to nobody, holds no contact grant, and MUST NOT be handed the consent in a form it can read.

gist: A forwarder serves openly key records, identity occurrences and the routes of unowned nodes (itself, a bare server), which carry no person.
entry_phrase: What it serves openly is what it served before:

gist: A responder serves a stranger the announced testimony (binding, key records, public kinds) of any subject whose live federation-scope owner binding it holds, regardless of publish set; no owned route.
entry_phrase: A responder serves a stranger the announced testimony of any subject whose live federation-scope owner-binding it holds

gist: A forwarder holds about a pair only that a link between two announced endpoints crossed it, or ciphertext waiting in a mailbox for a sleeping peer, bounded in retention.
entry_phrase: What the forwarder holds about the pair is what

gist: A requester shows its route to the one it asks before consent, disclosing nothing the pre-seal route fetch does not already hand any dialler.
entry_phrase: A requester therefore shows its route to the one it asks before consent

gist: Consent is the acceptance itself: a route reaches a peer only from its owner and only a peer the owner addressed; no forwarder gate is needed or permitted.
entry_phrase: Consent is the acceptance itself: a route reaches a peer only from its owner and only a peer the owner addressed.

gist: A superseding route after contact is handed the same way the first was.
entry_phrase: A superseding route after contact is handed the same way the first was.

gist: Whether a peer answers a contact request is the peer's; the first-contact receiver order (per-sender, per-link, node-wide rate) is the anti-spam; a refused request gets no answer.
entry_phrase: Whether a peer answers a request is the peer's

gist: First contact under a flood is not promised; a client that cannot reach a peer says so rather than retrying on a fixed beat (jittered, not fixed).
entry_phrase: **What this does not promise:** first contact under a flood.

gist: The asked person may ignore a contact request: a private, local, undoable act of their own node; the asker is never told and sees exactly what a pending request shows.
entry_phrase: The asked person MAY ignore a request: a private, local, undoable act of their own node

gist: Either party may block the other: a private act of their own node; further requests from the blocked key are dropped unanswered, forwarder learning nothing; lifted only by its maker.
entry_phrase: Either party MAY block the other: a private act of their own node after which further requests from the blocked key are dropped without answer, the forwarder learning nothing, lifted only by the one who made it.

gist: The Anonymous Tier hides who published a federation-scope item from storing nodes, the directory and, with shaping, a network observer; packet layout, KDF label and AEAD not yet pinned.
entry_phrase: hides who published a federation-scope item from the nodes that store it, from the directory, and, with shaping, from an observer of the network.

gist: Anonymous mode is a property of a node, not of a publication: using the tier and being anonymous are one thing.
entry_phrase: Using the tier and being anonymous are one thing: **anonymous mode**, a property of a node and not of a publication.

gist: An anonymous node is a separate dedicated identity: fresh user key and node key, no self roster shared with and no row linking it to any announced identity.
entry_phrase: A node in anonymous mode is a **separate, dedicated identity**: a fresh user key and node key with no self roster shared with, and no row linking it to, any announced identity of the person.

gist: A person may later prove an anonymous identity and an announced one are both theirs by a signed statement under both keys, and is never found out otherwise.
entry_phrase: The person MAY later prove the two are theirs by a signed statement under both keys and is never found out otherwise.

gist: An anonymous node announces nothing, publishes everything at federation scope through the tier under publication keys, is reached only at its rendezvous, holds only shaped layer and rendezvous links.
entry_phrase: The node announces nothing, publishes everything at federation scope through the tier under the publication keys of item 9, and is reached only at its rendezvous (item 10).

gist: An anonymous node may be any device class, a phone on Wi-Fi included, and sends end-to-end cover packets by default at the item-8 rate.
entry_phrase: It MAY be any device class, a phone on Wi-Fi included.

gist: A node is anonymous from its first run or never: an announced node never enters anonymous mode and an anonymous node never announces; wanting both means two nodes.
entry_phrase: So an announced node never enters anonymous mode and an anonymous node never announces; a person who wants both runs two nodes.

gist: Anonymous mode is offered only when rooms can be carried through the tier; until then a client lists the mode and does not enable it.
entry_phrase: So until rooms ride the tier a client lists the mode and does not enable it.

gist: An anonymous node holds one identity; a person who wants two rooms kept apart runs two nodes; an ordinary node carries as many signers as it hosts.
entry_phrase: an anonymous node holds one identity, and a person who wants two rooms kept apart runs two nodes.

gist: In a room riding the tier an anonymous identity may hold moderate, takedown and review duties by the same appointment as any member; the holder is the node's identity.
entry_phrase: In a room that rides the tier an anonymous identity MAY hold the `moderate`, `takedown` and `review` duties of

gist: An anonymous moderation-duty holder is blocked, contested by reconsideration:{grounds}, revoked by the room and tracked by moderation_track_record as any holder is.
entry_phrase: so it is blocked, contested by `reconsideration:{grounds}`, revoked by the room and tracked by `moderation_track_record` as any holder is.

gist: An anonymous node is not a relay: it uses the tier and carries nothing for it, since a relay's route must be live and announced.
entry_phrase: it uses the tier and carries nothing for it.

gist: Every announced node that runs the substrate relays onion traffic for others by default, whether or not anyone on it uses the tier.
entry_phrase: Every announced node that runs the substrate relays onion traffic for others by default, whether or not anyone on it uses the tier.

gist: A node holding no serve seat may opt out of relaying by publishing the opt-out marker and withdrawing its hop key on the same superseding row.
entry_phrase: A node that holds no serve seat MAY opt out of relaying by publishing the opt-out marker of

gist: A serve node never opts out of relaying: a seat carrying the marker is out of conformance as seat_opted_out, and a seat without a valid hop key as seat_without_hop_key.
entry_phrase: A serve node MAY NOT: a seat carrying the marker is out of conformance as `seat_opted_out`, and a seat without a valid hop key as `seat_without_hop_key`.

gist: A node with no hop key and no marker is not yet capable of relaying and is simply not placed.
entry_phrase: A node with no hop key and no marker is not yet capable of relaying and is simply not placed.

gist: Device policy: a phone relays by default only on Wi-Fi while charging; the user may override either way, the client stating each cost; servers and homes relay by default.
entry_phrase: The user MAY override the policy either way, and the client states the cost of each setting.

gist: The tier carries federation-scope publication and rooms: anonymous members exchange a room's rows through the tier, each reaching its mailbox by own route; such a room is private, never public.
entry_phrase: The tier carries federation-scope publication, and it carries rooms.

gist: An onion packet is fixed-length and layered, each hop's layer encapsulated to that hop's X-Wing hop key; each hop removes one layer, learns only the next; one KEM ciphertext per hop.
entry_phrase: An onion packet is a layered packet of fixed length in which each hop's layer is encapsulated to that hop's X-Wing onion hop key

gist: Every onion layer is post-quantum: a construction whose per-hop key agreement is classical alone is not conformant.
entry_phrase: Every layer is post-quantum: a construction whose per-hop key agreement is classical alone is not conformant

gist: The onion packet's byte layout, KDF label and AEAD are pinned by this section from the implementer's submission with known answers in the verification library; residual at 1.13.3.1 until then.
entry_phrase: The packet's byte layout, key-derivation label and AEAD are pinned by this section from the implementer's submission, as every wire shape of this document is, with known answers carried by the verification library.

gist: The hop KEM is X-Wing as the normative reference defines it; another combiner over the same key shapes is another construction under another identifier.
entry_phrase: **The hop KEM is X-Wing as the normative reference defines it** ([X-Wing], the draft's combiner)

gist: The onion body is tagging-resistant: a hop that alters any byte leaves the packet unreadable at every later hop and at exit; wide-block satisfies, per-layer body seal does not.
entry_phrase: a hop that alters any byte of a packet's body MUST leave the packet unreadable at every later hop and at its exit.

gist: An onion route has exactly three hops, one from each of three layers.
entry_phrase: A route has exactly three hops, one from each of three layers.

gist: A relay for a period is a node whose signed transport_destination row is live and announced, with valid hop key and no opt-out marker, owner-bound under a bundle-charter root; unowned never.
entry_phrase: whose current signed `transport_destination` row is live and announced, carries a valid hop key and no opt-out marker,

gist: At use a relay's layer links are shaped and an unshaped link carries no onion packet; activating the tier turns shaping on for the node's layer links.
entry_phrase: At use, a relay's layer links MUST be shaped, and an unshaped link carries no onion packet.

gist: Relay links are standing shaped links assigned by hash from the fold; a route is a walk over them and nothing is dialled per route.
entry_phrase: Relay links are standing shaped links assigned by hash from the fold, so a sender can compute the graph and nothing is dialled per route.

gist: Hop one is a sticky guard from the sender's own consented contacts offering relay (two for reach), outside any room the route serves; with none, a serve seat.
entry_phrase: **Hop one is a sticky guard** chosen from the sender's own consented contacts that offer relay, two of them for reach, and outside any room the route serves.

gist: A guard is kept for as long as it answers, never rotated on a schedule.
entry_phrase: A guard is kept for as long as it answers, never rotated on a schedule

gist: A long-lived mailbox pins its second hop as well.
entry_phrase: **A long-lived mailbox pins its second hop as well**

gist: Other hops are drawn from the fold over standing links, filtered by the sender's local delivery probes (never a shared row), owner age from the witnessed head, one per owner.
entry_phrase: They are filtered by the sender's own delivery probes, which stay local and never become a shared row, by owner age read from the witnessed head, and by at most one relay per owner.

gist: There is no steward cap on who relays; the bound is per sender, not per layer.
entry_phrase: there is no steward cap on who relays

gist: Fewer than three answering relays in any position makes the tier unavailable for that period; the tier never runs thin.
entry_phrase: fewer than three answering relays in any position makes the tier unavailable for that period; the tier never runs thin.

gist: A relay counts as answering when within the period it completed a shaped handshake, answered a route request, forwarded a packet the next hop acknowledged, or returned a self-addressed probe.
entry_phrase: a relay counts as answering when it completed a shaped handshake, answered a route request, forwarded a packet the next hop acknowledged, or returned a self-addressed probe within the period.

gist: The tier is available at a node when the floor holds on the deal (else onion_tier_unavailable_floor) and at least three relays per layer answer (else onion_tier_unavailable_liveness); the client shows counts.
entry_phrase: The tier is available at a node when the floor holds on the deal (else `onion_tier_unavailable_floor`) and at least three relays per layer are answering (else `onion_tier_unavailable_liveness`).

gist: Every tier rule is a pure function of the fold, never of arrival order: no coordinator assigns layers and two nodes holding the same rows deal the same layers.
entry_phrase: Every rule here is a pure function of the fold, never of arrival order, so no coordinator assigns the layers and two nodes holding the same rows deal the same layers.

gist: Onion packets travel as bodies of shaped frames; a longer packet is fragmented and reassembled at the next hop at the packet's own constant length; each hop a sealed attributed link.
entry_phrase: Onion packets travel as the bodies of shaped frames

gist: The storage node sees the last relay, never the publisher.
entry_phrase: the storage node sees the last relay, never the publisher.

gist: A receiver accepting targeted anonymous delivery publishes its route as a rendezvous:route:v1 row signed by a fresh rendezvous key each hour, the route reused within that hour.
entry_phrase: A receiver that accepts targeted anonymous delivery publishes the route to itself as a `rendezvous:route:v1` row

gist: For federation-scope targeted delivery the rendezvous node holding the receiver's mailbox is a serve seat; one seat holds each mailbox, hour-scale ciphertext only.
entry_phrase: For federation-scope targeted delivery the rendezvous node that holds the receiver's mailbox MUST be a serve seat.

gist: A room's mailbox is two member-owned always-on nodes chosen by the room, each holding the full row set, placed by replication consent; with none, a seat (two-hour wake warning).
entry_phrase: For a room, the mailbox is **two member-owned always-on nodes chosen by the room**

gist: A phone is never a mailbox and never a hop a reused route runs through; a route through a sleeping node is lost.
entry_phrase: A phone is never a mailbox and never a hop a reused route runs through; a route through a sleeping node is lost.

gist: A sender builds its own three-hop header from the directory's hop keys and appends the receiver's route.
entry_phrase: A sender builds its own three-hop header from the directory's hop keys and appends the receiver's route.

gist: Hop keys, layer assignments and rendezvous indexes rotate on global clocks, never on group events.
entry_phrase: Hop keys, layer assignments and rendezvous indexes rotate on global clocks, never on group events.

gist: End-to-end cover (a steady rate of packets to a random relay) is on by default for an anonymous node, costing about a third of a home's shaped share.
entry_phrase: The cover is a steady rate of packets to a random relay that is on by default for an anonymous node and costs about a third of a home's shaped share.

gist: User-facing copy says the anonymity set is small when few users share a relay; shaping is a prerequisite of the tier.
entry_phrase: with few users per relay the anonymity set is small, and user-facing copy says so

gist: A federation-scope item published through the tier is signed by a fresh hybrid pseudonym key whose key:record:v1 travels inline, identity_type pseudonym, no occurrence, no standing, refused as an identity.
entry_phrase: It is a fresh hybrid key pair whose `key:record:v1` travels inline, of `identity_type` `pseudonym`, with no occurrence and no standing

gist: A reader composes a pseudonym's rows as a stranger's; no ring signature, a sender is never unattributed; a person may later bind a pseudonym to themselves by a signed row.
entry_phrase: A reader composes its rows as a stranger's

gist: An anonymous peer is reached at its rendezvous route and answers a contact request through its own circuit; a route held for an announced contact is its circuit's exit, never dialled.
entry_phrase: It is reached at its rendezvous route, it answers a contact request through its own circuit

gist: The direct-link contact exchange never runs over a circuit and a forwarder offers no reflexive address on one; announced-to-anonymous contact never goes direct, and the announced peer's client says so.
entry_phrase: The direct-link exchange of the contact rule above never runs over a circuit, and a forwarder offers no reflexive address on one.

gist: For any future multi-hop amendment, rotation clocks are global, never group-event-driven.
entry_phrase: rotation clocks must be global, never group-event-driven.

gist: The section decides what the network is told about a destination, a device and a publisher: which destinations are announced, which devices are listed, who is handed a route, how a publisher stays unnamed
entry_phrase: This section decides what the network is told about a destination, a device and a publisher

gist: A person's device roster is public because it has to be for them to be contactable and follows the lightnet/darknet split one node at a time; each node's setup chooses whether that node announces
entry_phrase: it follows this section's lightnet/darknet split **one node at a time**.

gist: The handed code names the unannounced node and its route; the sealed occurrence and binding need no transport destination of their own, are served by no public read, and are superseded at federation scope by an announce
entry_phrase: They need no transport destination of their own, are served by no forwarder and no public read, and are superseded at federation scope by an announce.

gist: Nothing in the genesis bundle or the holders' ceremony carries or seeds a seated node's owner-binding, which is the owner's own row
entry_phrase: nothing in the genesis bundle or the holders' ceremony carries or seeds the binding, which is the owner's own row.

gist: The self cohort over the owner-binding graph decides who reaches the unannounced remainder
entry_phrase: It is the `self` cohort over the owner-binding graph that decides who reaches the unannounced remainder.

gist: Two members of one group get unrelated addresses; a compromise of the record layer cannot recompute or link the addresses a node has used
entry_phrase: Two members of one group get unrelated addresses.

gist: An outside observer of link traffic sees each member node exists, link requests to 16-byte derived destinations it cannot map to a group or member, the identity of the node that opened each link, and sealed frames with timing and sizes; it cannot fetch the content
entry_phrase: For a group it sees link requests to 16-byte derived destinations that it cannot map to a group or a member, the identity of the node that opened each link, and then sealed frames with their timing and sizes.

gist: Outsiders here means the directory and any reader of wire identifiers; that some group exists, from traffic and federation-tier hard_case events, is the non-goal of CC 1.13.3.1
entry_phrase: *Outsiders* here means the directory and any reader of wire identifiers

gist: No directed announce can satisfy the purposive sentence: multi-hop path learning is outsider observation, and a rotating derived destination emits a re-announce wave while a non-rotating one leaves a removed member holding every peer's addressing
entry_phrase: One that does not rotate leaves a removed member holding every peer's addressing indefinitely

gist: Announce-free reach (direct link; relay-blinded resolution) is the sanctioned posture
entry_phrase: Announce-free reach (direct link; relay-blinded resolution) is the sanctioned posture.

gist: A forwarder on a ridden identity-plane link learns only what CC 1.13.3.1 concedes at federation scope: it cannot read the body, cannot tell a room body from a replication round, and holds no identifier that names the room
entry_phrase: It cannot read the body, cannot tell a room body from a replication round, and holds no identifier that names the room.

gist: A forwarder carrying a stream's chunks is handed no stream binding, which names the room; a stream's hello is a first guess the binding overrides, never the other way
entry_phrase: A stream's hello is a first guess the binding overrides, never the other way.

gist: What is conceded by forwarding is the CC 1.13.3.1 non-goal: an on-path observer correlating link traffic across a clique of members can infer that a group exists; blinded rotating retained state is reserved for the multi-hop amendment and a deployment that needs it layers it
entry_phrase: A deployment that needs it layers it.

gist: What a proxy learns is what was pulled from it, which the seat would have learned; the seat sees the proxy's pull and not the asker's
entry_phrase: What a proxy learns is what was pulled from it, which the seat would have learned.

gist: What is conceded is that a referred stranger learns a relay-offering node's route, and roughly where it is, without being a contact
entry_phrase: What is conceded is that a referred stranger learns such a node's route, and roughly where it is, without being a contact.

gist: The served set of a responder is the announced testimony and nothing more, an owned node's route never among it; first contact never waits on a host's refresh of its publish set
entry_phrase: The served set is this and nothing more, an owned node's route never among it.

gist: Under a flood an honest stranger's chance on one dial falls to about the budget over the flood's rate, and a stranger with no route row yet meets the smaller route-request budget first; nothing in the document keeps that chance up
entry_phrase: a stranger with no route row yet meets the smaller route-request budget first.

gist: An anonymous identity never shares its node's address with a public identity, because the guard sees the address
entry_phrase: What an anonymous identity never shares is its node's address with a public identity, because the guard sees the address.

gist: A room whose members are all anonymous operates only while one of them holds the moderate duty; such a room does without a legally reachable person behind the duty; its two-consent admission keeps a removed member out
entry_phrase: What such a room does without is a legally reachable person behind the duty.

gist: The chance that both ends of a route are hostile is the hostile share of the sender's own relay contacts times the hostile share of the fold; minting identities moves neither
entry_phrase: Minting identities moves neither, since a minted identity is nobody's contact.

gist: The client shows the answering-relay counts, which may differ between nodes; below ten per layer the client says the set is small
entry_phrase: below ten per layer the client says the set is small

gist: A relay can count the packets sent to one rendezvous in a period, because the route is reused within it; that count is what the mailbox seat learns
entry_phrase: What the mailbox seat learns is item 8's count.

gist: An insider of a private room who times a sleeping phone's messages, with an observer of when it is online, can narrow the sender over many messages; an anonymous identity is never in a public room, so the attacker must already be a member
entry_phrase: can narrow the sender over many messages.

gist: Position (informative): the design sits in the zero-emission corner of the anonymity trilemma; the two-plane split and determinism replacing coordination answer its two prices; a ballot process whose occurrence is invisible to outsiders below federation is a corollary
entry_phrase: This design sits in the zero-emission corner of the anonymity trilemma

gist: Each node sends one census return per period; two aggregators fold them into one mesh census per class, published as levels never changes; no single aggregator reads a return
entry_phrase: Each node sends one **census return** per period. Two aggregators fold the returns of a period into one **mesh census** per class. The census is published as levels, never as changes. No single aggregator can read a return, and only the two aggregators of a period acting together could.

gist: A census return is sent once per period by a node whose owner binding chains to a bundle root
entry_phrase: A return is sent once per period by a node whose owner-binding chains to a bundle root ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)).

gist: Counts of voices count owners, never nodes; counts of the mesh count nodes, at most eight per owner
entry_phrase: Counts of voices — the expected-active base, a tally — count **owners**, never nodes. Counts of the mesh — nodes, links, rows held — count nodes, at most eight per owner.

gist: The census period is the global cadence of the constant tick
entry_phrase: The period is the global cadence of the constant tick ([CC 5.4.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.5)).

gist: A return is sent at an offset derived from H(return_token, period) at one fixed size; on a shaped link it replaces a cover frame
entry_phrase: A return is sent at an offset derived from `H(return_token ‖ period)`, at one fixed size, so its timing and size carry nothing about the node's activity. On a shaped link ([CC 5.4.3](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.3)) it replaces a cover frame.

gist: Every return field is a one-hot vector over log2 buckets, bucket = bit_length(v), 0 in bucket 0; the registered aggregation_algorithm_id layout is authoritative for the index
entry_phrase: Every field of a return is a one-hot vector over its log2 buckets, indexed once: `bucket = bit_length(v)`, with `0` in bucket `0`. So a count of 2 000 rows is a 1 in bucket 11 and a 0 elsewhere, and 2 048 is bucket 12. The layout the registered `aggregation_algorithm_id` names is authoritative for the index.

gist: Each return vector is split into two additive shares over a prime field, one per aggregator, with a linear validity proof checked jointly (Prio3 histogram); neither aggregator sees a return
entry_phrase: The node splits each vector into two additive shares over a prime field and sends each share to a different aggregator, with a share of a fully linear validity proof. The two aggregators check that proof jointly — every entry 0 or 1, the entries summing to 1 — without either learning the vector (the Prio3 histogram construction of the VDAF family). Neither aggregator sees any node's return.

gist: A valid return adds exactly one count to exactly one bucket per field (the stuffing ceiling, enforced not trusted)
entry_phrase: A valid return adds exactly one count to exactly one bucket per field — the stuffing ceiling, enforced rather than trusted.

gist: A partial (census:partial:{class}:v1) is a public federation row signed by the seat, one per (seat, class, period): field-wise sum of accepted shares, count summed, commitment over accepted tokens
entry_phrase: Each aggregator publishes a **partial** — `census:partial:{class}:v1`, a public federation row signed by the seat, one per (seat, class, period). The partial is the field-wise sum of the shares the aggregator accepted, the count of shares it summed, and a commitment over the accepted tokens.

gist: The composite is partial_a plus partial_b element-wise and names both partials; the door checks cells sum to mass_total and mass_total equals the partials' sum, refusing on mismatch
entry_phrase: The **composite** is `partial_a + partial_b` element-wise in the field and names both partials. The door checks exactly, in the field, that the cells sum to `mass_total` and that `mass_total = partial_a + partial_b` (`census_composite_mass_total_mismatch`, `census_composite_partials_mismatch`).

gist: A composite with fewer than k = 10 sources is refused (census_composite_below_k)
entry_phrase: The door refuses a composite with fewer than **k = 10** sources (`census_composite_below_k`).

gist: On a census composite n_eff = source_count by construction and the dominance gate checks the aggregators; max_source_multiplicity is 1 by construction and the door refuses any other value
entry_phrase: Because every accepted return from one owner contributes mass 1, `n_eff = source_count` by construction, and the dominance gate of [CC 6.1.2.1.2](#6.1.2.1.2) runs over the composite's members as a check on the aggregators. The multiplicity gate of [CC 6.1.2.1](#6.1.2.1) runs on the composite as on every v3 object and never binds. That is because `max_source_multiplicity` is `1` on every census composite by construction (one return per owner is one source, and a secret-shared seat never sees a payload it could measure similarity on) and the census door refuses any other value.

gist: A census:share row is addressed: a row whose signed for_key_id names one recipient is held by author and recipient only, served to the recipient only, never widened; others refuse it
entry_phrase: A return rides `census:share:{class}:v1`, one row per aggregator, **addressed**: a row whose signed `for_key_id` names one recipient is held by the author's node and the recipient's node and by no other. The serve gate sends it to the recipient only, and no widening ever applies to it. Any other node offered it refuses it at its receive door as `federation_addressed_not_recipient`.

gist: A share row expires at the period's end and is reaped
entry_phrase: The share row expires at the period's end and is reaped.

gist: A share's for_key_id must name a serve seat (census_return_recipient_not_seat); the sender draws the pair by H(period, class) but the door never checks membership in the drawn pair
entry_phrase: The pair drawn from the seats by `H(period ‖ class)` is the honest sender's rule. The door checks only that `for_key_id` names a serve seat, refusing otherwise (`census_return_recipient_not_seat`), never membership in the drawn pair.

gist: Partial and composite rows are federation-scope; the composite is a 2.1 scores row whose signed members (version=3, source_count, n_eff, multiplicity, both commitments, algorithm id) pass the dominance gate at admission
entry_phrase: The partial is `census:partial:{class}:v1` and the composite `census:composite:{class}:v1`, both federation-scope rows. The composite is a [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.1) `scores` row (the exception [CC 6.1.3](#6.1.3) names) whose signed members are the inputs of [CC 6.1.2.1](#6.1.2.1) (`version = 3`, `source_count`, `n_eff`, `max_source_multiplicity`, `mass_commitment_hex`, `member_commitment_hex`, `aggregation_algorithm_id`), verified at federation admission by the dominance gate.

gist: An aggregator deletes a share once summed into its partial, holds no share past the period's end, and keeps partials and composites for a bounded number of periods per class
entry_phrase: An aggregator MUST delete a share once it is summed into its partial and MUST hold no share past the period's end. It keeps partials and composites for a bounded number of periods per class.

gist: A composite is a histogram per field per cell; readers compute the median bucket and trimmed statistics; a relief reads the median; display rounding is presentation only
entry_phrase: A composite is a histogram per field per cell. A reader computes the median bucket and the trimmed statistics from it, and a relief reads the median. The published rows carry exact field sums. A reader's display MAY round a derived value to a coarse grid (two significant figures, so 47 shows as 50 and 23 500 as 24 000). That rounding is a presentation convention, never a property of a published row.

gist: Suppression is the k floor at the door: a cell under 10 owners is merged upward and withheld (census_composite_below_k); regions are self-declared, continent-sized at most
entry_phrase: Suppression is the k floor at the door: a cell with fewer than **k = 10** owners is merged upward and then withheld as *below the floor* (`census_composite_below_k`). Regions are self-declared and continent-sized at most, and are published only where the floor holds.

gist: A composite publishes levels never deltas, carries per-period tokens never node ids; the directory holds no census data; differential-privacy noise is an optional layer
entry_phrase: A composite publishes levels, never deltas. It carries per-period tokens, never node ids. The directory holds no census data. Differential-privacy noise on small cells is an optional layer a deployment MAY add.

gist: No return carries anything about the Anonymous Tier: no routes, onion packets or bytes; relay standing and opt-out return only as floored counts per class per region; onion users never
entry_phrase: **No return carries anything about the Anonymous Tier** ([CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.4.6)). There is no field for routes built, onion packets sent, relayed or received, or onion bytes. Onion traffic is never a plane in a return. Relay standing, hop-key publication and opt-out are returned only as counts per class per coarse region under the floor. That publishes nothing a reader could not compute from the public layer deal. Onion **users** are never counted, in any form.

gist: A community's expected-active count is member-only: each member's cell carries its recent bit (active within four periods), sealed under the community epoch key, sent to two members
entry_phrase: A community's expected-active count is a member-only composite. Each member's period return carries one cell per community it belongs to (the owner's own *recent* bit). The bit is set when the owner was active in this period or any of the previous three. It is not something recoverable from a sum. The cell is sealed under the community's epoch key and sent, as `census:member:share:v1`, to two **members** of that community drawn from its roster by `H(group_exporter_secret ‖ period)`.

gist: census:expected_active:v1 is the count of owners with the recent bit set, recomputed by every member from the two partials; a row differing from a member's recomputation is refused
entry_phrase: The two publish `census:member:partial:v1` into the room, and `census:expected_active:v1` is the count of owners whose recent bit is set, recomputed by every member from the two partials. A row whose count or floor flag differs from a member's own recomputation is refused `census_expected_active_mismatch`.

gist: The governance base falls at most a tenth per period, never below its floor: the roster at the policy count minimum, else the larger of rooted-active members and half the
entry_phrase: The base falls by at most a tenth per period: `base_t · 10 ≥ base_{t−1} · 9`, so a larger fall is clipped to `⌈base_{t−1} · 9 / 10⌉`. It never falls below its **floor**. The floor is the standing roster at or below the count minimum of the [CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13) policy table. Above it, the floor is the larger of the roster's rooted-active members and half of the last stable count, `⌈lastStable / 2⌉`.

gist: A fall of more than a third in one period freezes the base; the first period returning at least two thirds of the pre-fall count releases it and the ratchet
entry_phrase: A fall of the count by more than a third in one period (`ea · 3 < prev · 2`, `ea` the period's count and `prev` the count before it) is read as a partition. The base then freezes where it stood. It is released by the first period whose count is at least two thirds of the count before the fall (`ea · 3 ≥ ref · 2`, `ref` that count). The ratchet resumes from there.

entry_phrase: A governance act — an `objection:{state}` row, a roster change, a policy amendment under [CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13) — is an identified row counted against the census base. It is never secret.

entry_phrase: Separately, a community MAY hold a **secret poll or election** in the same instrument, at its own discretion. gist: FedCode is the one human-shareable shorthand for a key_id; every implementation renders and parses the same code for the same key
entry_phrase: **FedCode** is the **one** human-shareable shorthand: a compact, QR-able, checksummed render of a federation entity's identity for **bootstrap UX**. It is pinned here so **every implementation renders and parses the same code for the same key**. That is a cross-impl determinism requirement of the same class as [CC 2.6.3](#2.6.3) hex / [CC 2.6.1](#2.6.1) JCS.

gist: FedCode is a deterministic render of an existing key_id, not a new envelope field; its kind byte is a payload discriminator; resolution is DNS-free
entry_phrase: FedCode is a deterministic render of an existing `key_id`, **not** a new envelope field. It is additive on the frozen 1+4 surface. The `kind` byte is a payload discriminator of the same discipline as `subject_kind` riding the single `scores` shape ([CC 3.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)). Resolution is **DNS-free**.

entry_phrase: The reference implementation is CIRISVerify; every other component decodes through it.

gist: FedCode kinds are 1=user 2=agent 3=node 4=family 5=community, mapping 1:1 onto identity_type; NodeCode v1 is kind node
entry_phrase: The v1 **NodeCode** (`CIRIS-V1-`) renders a *node's* key and is retained as `kind: node`. The code is tied to the **entity** — five kinds mapping 1:1 onto [CC 3.4.7.1](part_3_the_namespace.md) `identity_type` and the rostered `subject_kind`s:

gist: A user code with no nodes resolves through the federation directory by walking nodes_owned_by(U); a code carrying nodes resolves with no directory
entry_phrase: A code that carries them resolves with no directory — pairing, a QR across a table, an air-gapped hand-off. A code that carries none resolves through the **federation directory**. The consumer walks `nodes_owned_by(U)`

gist: nodes_owned_by is the exact inverse of owner_of, held by construction
entry_phrase: `nodes_owned_by(U)` — the exact inverse of `owner_of` ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md); `n ∈ nodes_owned_by(U)` iff `owner_of(n) == U`, held by construction)

entry_phrase: to find the nodes to transport to, **as visible to the walker**. A peer outside `U`'s `self` cohort holds only `U`'s federation-scoped owner-bindings ([CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md) audience rule), so the directory walk yields exactly the announced roster of [CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md), while `U`'s own nodes see every binding.

entry_phrase: A node whose owner resolves ambiguous is **skipped, not fatal**: one poisoned node must not make its owner unroutable, while a direct query about that node still fails closed.

gist: FedCode wire form: binary payload, CRC-16-CCITT (0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no final xor) 2 bytes big-endian, RFC 4648 base32 unpadded, version prefix, 4-character dash groups for display; QR form ungrouped
entry_phrase: Binary payload, then **CRC-16-CCITT** (polynomial `0x1021`, init `0xFFFF`, no final xor) appended as 2 bytes big-endian, then **RFC 4648 base32** (alphabet `A–Z2–7`, padding stripped on encode, re-padded on decode). The result is prefixed by the version token and grouped into 4-character dash-separated chunks for display; the QR form is ungrouped.

gist: Decoders normalize (drop whitespace, upper-case, strip dashes) and accept the undashed prefix; length-prefixed fields are 1-byte length, at most 255 UTF-8 bytes; overflow is malformed
entry_phrase: Decoders normalize (drop whitespace, upper-case, strip dashes) and accept the undashed prefix. All length-prefixed fields are 1-byte length, ≤ 255 UTF-8 bytes; an overflow is malformed.

gist: v2 payload: version 0x02, kind, sha256(key_id), ed25519 pubkey, LP(key_id), transport/alias/group hints; v3 adds node_count (0..16), per-node LP(key_id) + transport key, then a presence-tagged PQC commitment
entry_phrase: version(1)=0x02 | kind(1) | sha256(key_id)(32) | ed25519_pubkey(32)

gist: A decoder verifies the payload's sha256(key_id) against the key_id; the v1 layout is retained unchanged under CIRIS-V1-
entry_phrase: `sha256(key_id)` binds the display `key_id` into the CRC-protected payload — a decoder MUST verify it against `key_id`. The v1 layout is retained unchanged: `version=0x01 | key_id_hash(32) | pubkey(32) | LP(key_id_str) | LP(transport_hint) | LP(alias_hint) | crc16` under `CIRIS-V1-`.

entry_phrase: **Constraints (each MUST be enforced at encoder AND decoder — a code minted by another implementation is exactly the case an encoder cannot police).**

gist: An embedded node key is the node's transport Ed25519, never a federation key; a code whose embedded transport key equals the owner's pubkey is rejected
entry_phrase: 1. **An embedded node key is the node's TRANSPORT Ed25519 — never the owner's federation key, never the node's federation key.**

entry_phrase: 3. **`node_count ≤ 16` and total payload ≤ 1024 bytes before base32.**

entry_phrase: A code with no nodes and no commitment MUST encode as **v2, byte-identically**, so nothing already issued moves; only a non-empty tail emits `CIRIS-V3-`.

gist: v1 decodes as kind node; v2 decodes unchanged; a v3 decoder accepts all three prefixes; a v2-only decoder rejects CIRIS-V3- outright
entry_phrase: v1 decodes as `kind: node`; v2 decodes unchanged; a v3 decoder accepts all three prefixes; a v2-only decoder MUST reject `CIRIS-V3-` outright rather than mis-parse it — the prefix differs before any payload byte is read.

entry_phrase: **(a)** The host admits the classical half plus the commitment, fetches the ML-DSA body through the existing Key Pull, and verifies it against the commitment **before** writing a hybrid record. entry_phrase: **(b)** The commitment applies to **any** kind of code — a plain `user` code with no nodes emits v3 with `node_count = 0`.

gist: A FedCode is unsigned; a commitment match is never treated as authentication of the identity; a code with no commitment fails closed at the pull check
entry_phrase: **(e)** A FedCode is **unsigned**: the commitment inherits exactly the trust of the code carrying it and adds no authority. A hyphenated spelling of this name is not byte-equal to this string and is a non-conformant alias, not a match. |

gist: Producer, substrate and every consumer MUST serialize and match the exact wrap_algorithm wire string; MUST NOT normalize case or separators; a variant spelling is unknown under fail-secure decode
entry_phrase: A producer, the substrate, and every consumer MUST serialize/deserialize the exact string above. A mismatch silently fails grant decode (same hazard class as the [CC 5.3.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) STREAM-nonce `epoch` encoding). Both rows above are the frozen snake_case forms. A case-, separator- or ordering-variant of either (`x25519-mlkem768-aes256-gcm-hkdf-sha256` and its kin) is an **unknown** `wrap_algorithm` under the fail-secure decode rule below, never a normalizable alias. A consumer MUST NOT normalize case or separators before comparison, per the [CC 5.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) one-construction-one-identifier rule.

gist: Consumers MUST reject an unknown wrap_algorithm string (fail-secure); new algorithms are additive rows
entry_phrase: Consumers MUST reject an unknown `wrap_algorithm` string (fail-secure). That is exactly what makes the addition safe: old consumers refuse v3 grants rather than mis-decoding them.

gist: Every CC 3.3.2 closed set serializes and matches its lowercase snake_case wire string exactly; the PascalCase variant never appears on the wire; no case, separator or ordering normalization
entry_phrase: - The **wire string** is lowercase-ASCII `snake_case`, is the serialized value, and satisfies the [CC 5.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) identifier class rule. A producer, the substrate and every consumer MUST serialize and match **exactly these bytes**, and MUST NOT normalize case, separators or ordering before comparison.

entry_phrase: Where the two readings could diverge, the wire-string column governs. Where a future row is added, its wire string is derived the same way the rows above are (PascalCase word boundaries → `_`, lowercased, digits staying attached to the token they qualify). That string is pinned in the table rather than recomputed by an implementation.

entry_phrase: a `withdraws` or `recants` naming a `key_grant` row is refused; once shared, always shared at the wire layer, and forward secrecy is by rotation ([CC 4.4.3.4.5](part_4_composition_governance.md), [CC 5.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md))

entry_phrase: the row is placed at the content's scope and reaches the recipient's node because the row *refers to* it ([CC 6.1.5.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md)). The key follows the bytes to exactly the device it is for, which is the point. A device merely named in a wrap is not thereby delivered anything else.

entry_phrase: A wrap is not a grant of authority and is never read as one. Admission of the *content* it opens is governed by the cohort roster, and issuance authority by [CC 2.4.1.2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md).

entry_phrase: There is no multi-wrap set. A `key_grant:{axis}:v1` row carries one wrap for one recipient, and there is no carrier class ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)).

gist: Rotation after recipient compromise: new key_grant rows for remaining recipients under a new axis identity with rotation_chain naming prior rows; no row supersedes or withdraws the prior wrap
entry_phrase: when a publisher rotates the keys a compromised recipient held, it re-seals under fresh keys and emits **new `key_grant:{axis}:v1` rows for the remaining recipients**. Each new row is under a new axis identity (a re-sealed blob's `at_rest_sha256`, a new epoch), with `rotation_chain` naming the prior rows for the pair as a trail. No row supersedes or removes the prior wrap. The compromised recipient is simply absent from the new rows. This rotation is never a `withdraws` against the prior row: `withdraws` is the holders-directory eviction primitive in [CC 5.3.2.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md), and a `withdraws` naming a `key_grant` row is refused above.
